topic: The 2026 JFK Files — What 11,022 New Pages Actually Revealed
photo_prompt: Document archive boxes, official government release setting
heading: 62 YEARS LATER. 11,022 NEW PAGES. HERE'S WHAT THE GOVERNMENT JUST ADMITTED.
photo_note: This is a 2026 current-events photo. Use an official White House/National Archives press photo (search Wikimedia Commons + flag as government work = public domain) or a generic document/archive stock image instead of a copyrighted news photo.
confirmed: On January 30, 2026, the National Archives released 11,022 additional pages (140 PDF files) of JFK assassination records, following President Trump's January 2025 Executive Order 14176 mandating full declassification. This followed an earlier March 2025 release that made all previously withheld JFK files public.
disputed: Researchers are still combing through the newly released material. Some independent researchers claim the new pages support long-standing questions about CIA knowledge of Lee Harvey Oswald before the assassination — official agencies maintain the core Warren Commission findings (Oswald acted alone) still stand. No new pages released so far have produced a change in the official conclusion.
caption:
On January 30, 2026, the National Archives released 11,022 additional pages of JFK assassination records — the latest step in a declassification process ordered by President Trump's January 2025 executive order.

This followed an earlier March 2025 release that made all previously withheld JFK files public for the first time in 62 years.

**What's confirmed: the documents are real and have been released. What's disputed: whether anything in them changes the official 1964 Warren Commission conclusion that Oswald acted alone — researchers are still analyzing the material, and no agency has announced a revised conclusion.**

Source: National Archives (archives.gov/research/jfk), Executive Order 14176. Follow for more. 🧵

topic: The Magic Bullet — One Bullet, Seven Wounds, Three Direction Changes
photo_prompt: Trajectory diagram style image, clinical/forensic documentary framing
heading: ONE BULLET. SEVEN WOUNDS. THREE DIRECTION CHANGES. THE GOVERNMENT CALLED IT POSSIBLE.
photo_note: This requires only a diagram/trajectory illustration, not a photo of real people — low copyright risk, can use an original illustration or AI-generated diagram instead of any real photo.
confirmed: The Warren Commission's 1964 single-bullet theory holds that one bullet caused 7 wounds across JFK and Texas Governor John Connally, changing direction multiple times, and was later found in near-pristine condition on a stretcher at Parkland Hospital. This is the official, formally adopted explanation.
disputed: Independent ballistics experts, including some consulted by later congressional investigations (the 1979 House Select Committee on Assassinations), have raised persistent technical questions about the bullet's trajectory and condition. The 1979 House Committee itself concluded a 'probable conspiracy' existed based on acoustic evidence — a finding later disputed by the National Academy of Sciences in 1982, which found the acoustic evidence unreliable. The matter remains officially unresolved at the level of certainty either side claims.
caption:
The Warren Commission's official explanation for JFK's assassination requires a single bullet to have caused 7 separate wounds across two men, changing direction three times, then turning up in near-pristine condition.

**What's confirmed: this is the government's own official adopted theory, and the bullet's condition is documented. What's disputed: independent ballistics experts have raised technical questions for decades, and even a 1979 congressional committee found a 'probable conspiracy' — though that finding was itself later disputed by the National Academy of Sciences in 1982.**

Source: Warren Commission Report 1964, House Select Committee on Assassinations 1979, National Academy of Sciences 1982. Follow for more. 🧵

topic: JFK Fired Allen Dulles. Then Dulles Investigated JFK's Own Murder.
heading: JFK FIRED HIM. THEN HE WAS APPOINTED TO INVESTIGATE JFK'S OWN MURDER.
photo_note: 1960s-era CIA official photos are often US government-produced and may be public domain — verify on Wikimedia Commons under 'Allen Dulles' before use; if uncertain, use a CIA seal/headquarters image instead.
confirmed: Allen Dulles served as CIA Director until November 1961, when President Kennedy removed him following the failed Bay of Pigs invasion — JFK reportedly said he wanted to 'splinter the CIA into a thousand pieces.' In 1963, after Kennedy's assassination, President Johnson appointed Dulles to the Warren Commission, the body investigating JFK's death.
disputed: Critics, including some historians and later congressional researchers, have pointed to this as a documented conflict of interest — a man removed by Kennedy investigating Kennedy's own murder, with access to CIA information the Commission itself did not fully receive. The Warren Commission's findings have never been formally invalidated, but the appointment itself is widely cited as a structural weakness in the investigation's independence.
caption:
In November 1961, President Kennedy removed Allen Dulles as CIA Director following the failed Bay of Pigs invasion.

In 1963, after Kennedy was assassinated, Dulles was appointed to the Warren Commission — the body investigating JFK's own murder.

**What's confirmed: both the firing and the appointment are documented historical fact, not theory. What's disputed: whether this conflict of interest affected the investigation's conclusions — historians differ, and the Commission's findings were never formally overturned.**

Source: CIA historical records, Warren Commission archives. Follow for more. 🧵

topic: The Missing Autopsy Materials — A Documented Chain-of-Custody Gap
photo_prompt: Government records storage / archive box documentary image
heading: THE GOVERNMENT'S OWN REVIEW BOARD CONFIRMED KEY AUTOPSY MATERIALS WERE MISSING.
photo_note: Use a generic archive/records room stock image — no real identifiable person needed for this topic.
confirmed: The Assassination Records Review Board (ARRB), a federal body established by Congress in 1992, formally documented in its findings that certain original autopsy photographs and X-rays could not be located or verified against the original 1963 autopsy records, and that the chain of custody for key materials had gaps. This is a documented federal finding, not a theory.
disputed: The ARRB itself did not conclude this proved a conspiracy — its mandate was to document records issues, not determine guilt. Independent researchers have offered competing explanations ranging from simple mishandling to deliberate alteration; no consensus exists on which explanation is correct, and the ARRB's own report stopped short of endorsing any specific theory.
caption:
The Assassination Records Review Board — a federal body created by Congress — formally documented in the 1990s that key JFK autopsy photographs and X-rays had unexplained gaps in their chain of custody.

**What's confirmed: this is a documented finding from an official federal review board, not speculation. What's disputed: the ARRB itself did not conclude this proved any deliberate alteration — independent researchers disagree on the explanation, and no consensus exists.**

Source: Assassination Records Review Board final report, 1998. Follow for more. 🧵

topic: Tupac Shakur — The Trial Is Finally Happening. 30 Years Later.
heading: 30 YEARS. ONE SUSPECT. THE TRIAL FINALLY STARTS THIS AUGUST.
photo_note: 1990s Tupac photos are almost certainly owned by photo agencies (Getty, AP). Do not use a direct photo — recommend a symbolic image instead (a Las Vegas street scene, a court building) to avoid copyright risk.
confirmed: Duane 'Keffe D' Davis was arrested in September 2023 — 27 years after Tupac Shakur's September 1996 murder — and charged with first-degree murder. Prosecutors allege Davis orchestrated the drive-by shooting in retaliation for an earlier casino altercation. His trial, after multiple delays, is currently scheduled for August 10, 2026.
disputed: Davis has given inconsistent accounts over the years — admitting involvement in his own 2019 memoir and television interviews, then later claiming those statements were 'for entertainment purposes' after his arrest. His defense argues he wasn't present at the shooting and has pointed to alternative suspects. As of mid-2026, the case remains unresolved and no verdict has been reached.
caption:
30 years after Tupac Shakur's murder, the only person ever charged in the case is finally headed to trial.

Duane 'Keffe D' Davis was arrested in September 2023. His trial — delayed multiple times — is currently set for August 10, 2026.

**What's confirmed: Davis is charged, has pleaded not guilty, and the trial date is real and public record. What's disputed: guilt itself — Davis has given inconsistent accounts over the years, and as of now no verdict has been reached.**

Source: Clark County District Court records, ABC News, Associated Press. Follow for more. 🧵

heading: HE WROTE IT IN HIS OWN BOOK. NOW HE SAYS IT WAS JUST FOR ENTERTAINMENT.

caption:
Duane Davis described details of Tupac Shakur's murder — including providing the gun used — in his own 2019 memoir and in recorded interviews.

heading: A SEPARATE THEORY NAMES A DIFFERENT MUSIC MOGUL. HERE'S WHAT'S ACTUALLY BEEN CLAIMED.

Former LAPD detective Greg Kading and journalist Chuck Philips have both separately claimed a bounty was offered to gang members in connection with the 1996 shooting.

caption:
In 2024, reports surfaced that Tupac's family was investigating a possible link between his 1996 murder and music executive Sean 'Diddy' Combs.

topic: Princess Diana — What the Official Investigation Actually Found
heading: THE OFFICIAL INVESTIGATION TOOK YEARS. HERE'S EXACTLY WHAT IT CONCLUDED.
photo_note: Diana photos are almost universally owned by major photo agencies (Getty, PA, AP). Do not use a direct photo — recommend a Paris tunnel/bridge symbolic image or a formal government inquiry building image instead.
confirmed: Operation Paget, a three-year UK police investigation completed in 2006, concluded Princess Diana's death in a August 1997 Paris car crash was a tragic accident caused by chauffeur Henri Paul driving at high speed while intoxicated, combined with the car being pursued by paparazzi. A 2008 inquest jury formally ruled the deaths were 'unlawful killing' — specifically due to the grossly negligent driving of the following vehicles and Paul, not murder.
disputed: Despite the official conclusion, surveys have repeatedly found a significant share of the public still believes the crash was not accidental — a belief Operation Paget specifically investigated and found no credible evidence to support. The persistence of the theory despite a formal, multi-year police investigation is itself part of what makes this an enduring case study in conspiracy belief.
caption:
Operation Paget — a three-year official UK police investigation completed in 2006 — concluded Princess Diana's death was a tragic accident: a drunk driver at high speed, pursued by paparazzi.

A 2008 inquest jury ruled 'unlawful killing' due to grossly negligent driving — not murder.

**What's confirmed: this is the formal, completed conclusion of an extensive official investigation. What's disputed: polls have repeatedly shown a large share of the public still doesn't accept this conclusion, despite Paget specifically investigating and rejecting murder theories.**

Source: Operation Paget Report 2006, 2008 Inquest verdict. Follow for more. 🧵

topic: The Diana Letter — What She Actually Wrote, and What's Disputed About It
photo_prompt: Handwritten letter / document close-up style image
heading: SHE ALLEGEDLY WROTE DOWN WHO WOULD HARM HER. HERE'S THE FULL CONTEXT.
photo_note: Use a generic handwritten letter / vintage stationery close-up image — no real person's face needed, lower copyright risk.
confirmed: Diana's former butler, Paul Burrell, produced a note in 1997 that he said Diana wrote in October 1996, expressing fear about her safety. The existence and content of this note were formally examined during the 2008 inquest as part of the official evidence.
disputed: The inquest jury, after reviewing the note alongside all other evidence, did not find it sufficient to support a murder conclusion — they ruled unlawful killing was due to negligent driving, not an orchestrated plot. Critics have also raised questions about Burrell's credibility, given his own later admissions of inconsistencies in other statements he made about the royal household. The letter's existence is documented; what it proves remains contested.
caption:
A note allegedly written by Princess Diana in October 1996, produced by her former butler Paul Burrell, expressed fear for her safety.

The note was formally examined as evidence in the official 2008 inquest into her death.

**What's confirmed: the note exists and was examined as evidence — this is documented court record, not rumor. What's disputed: the inquest jury did not find it sufficient to support a murder conclusion, and questions have been raised about the source's broader credibility.**

Source: 2008 Inquest evidence record, Operation Paget Report. Follow for more. 🧵

topic: Marilyn Monroe — What the Official Ruling Says vs. Why Doubts Persist
heading: THE OFFICIAL RULING WAS 'PROBABLE SUICIDE.' THE INVESTIGATION FILE WAS SEALED FOR DECADES.
photo_note: Monroe photos are heavily copyrighted by photo agencies and her estate. Use a symbolic Hollywood-era image (a film reel, a vintage marquee) instead of a direct photo.
confirmed: The Los Angeles County Coroner's office officially ruled Marilyn Monroe's August 1962 death a 'probable suicide' from acute barbiturate poisoning, following a multi-day investigation. This remains the only official cause-of-death ruling ever issued.
disputed: Some files related to the case, including LAPD intelligence division records, remained sealed or were reportedly destroyed in subsequent decades, which has fueled persistent alternative theories. A 1982 review by the Los Angeles District Attorney's office, prompted by public pressure, found no evidence to support foul play and did not reopen the case. No subsequent official body has overturned the original ruling.
caption:
The Los Angeles County Coroner officially ruled Marilyn Monroe's 1962 death a 'probable suicide.' This remains the only official ruling ever issued.

**What's confirmed: this is the formal, unchanged legal conclusion. A 1982 District Attorney review also found no evidence of foul play. What's disputed: some related files were reportedly sealed or destroyed over the decades, which has kept alternative theories alive despite no official body ever overturning the ruling.**

Source: LA County Coroner's report 1962, LA District Attorney review 1982. Follow for more. 🧵

topic: MLK's Assassin Recanted. The King Family Won a Civil Trial Saying He Didn't Act Alone.
heading: THE SHOOTER CONFESSED. THEN HE TOOK IT BACK. THEN A JURY AGREED WITH THE FAMILY.
photo_note: 1960s civil rights movement photos vary in copyright status — many news agency photos are still protected. Search Wikimedia Commons specifically and verify; consider using a courthouse or document image instead if uncertain.
confirmed: James Earl Ray pleaded guilty to assassinating Martin Luther King Jr. in 1969, then recanted days later, claiming he was set up by a man he called 'Raoul,' and spent the rest of his life trying to withdraw his plea. In 1999, the King family brought a civil wrongful-death lawsuit; a Memphis jury found that King's assassination involved a broader conspiracy, not Ray acting alone — a verdict the King family has publicly stood behind.
disputed: The US Department of Justice conducted its own review in 2000 and concluded there was no reliable evidence of a wider conspiracy, disagreeing with the civil jury's finding. The two official conclusions — a civil jury verdict and a DOJ investigative review — directly contradict each other, and this contradiction has never been formally resolved.
caption:
James Earl Ray confessed to assassinating Martin Luther King Jr. in 1969, then recanted days later and spent the rest of his life trying to withdraw the plea.

In 1999, a Memphis civil jury — in a case brought by the King family — found the assassination involved a broader conspiracy, not Ray acting alone.

**What's confirmed: both the recantation and the 1999 civil verdict are real, documented legal outcomes. What's disputed: a 2000 Department of Justice review reached the opposite conclusion, finding no reliable evidence of a wider conspiracy — the two official findings directly contradict each other and neither has been formally overturned.**

Source: 1999 King v. Jowers civil trial record, DOJ 2000 investigative report. Follow for more. 🧵

topic: Amelia Earhart — 89 Years, No Confirmed Wreckage, Still Searching
photo_prompt: 1930s aviation documentary style, vintage aircraft imagery
heading: SHE VANISHED OVER THE PACIFIC IN 1937. NO CONFIRMED WRECKAGE HAS EVER BEEN FOUND.
photo_note: 1930s aviation photos of Earhart are generally public domain in the US — many official US government/Navy photos from her search are PD — search Wikimedia Commons and verify the specific image's tag.
confirmed: Amelia Earhart and navigator Fred Noonan disappeared on July 2, 1937, during an attempted round-the-world flight, somewhere over the central Pacific Ocean. The official US Navy and Coast Guard search at the time found no trace of the aircraft, and Earhart was declared legally dead in 1939.
disputed: Multiple organizations, including The International Group for Historic Aircraft Recovery (TIGHAR), have proposed theories ranging from a crash-landing on Nikumaroro Island to capture by Japanese forces. Various expeditions have reported possible debris or sonar anomalies over the decades, but none have been conclusively confirmed as belonging to Earhart's aircraft as of 2026. The case remains officially unsolved.
caption:
On July 2, 1937, Amelia Earhart and navigator Fred Noonan disappeared over the Pacific during an attempted round-the-world flight. No confirmed wreckage has ever been found.

**What's confirmed: the disappearance itself, and that official searches at the time found nothing. What's disputed: multiple competing theories exist about what happened, and several expeditions have reported possible leads over the decades — none confirmed as of 2026.**

Source: US Navy historical search records, TIGHAR research archive. Follow for more. 🧵

topic: Why These Cases Stay 'Unsolved' Even With Official Investigations
photo_prompt: Collage-style graphic of case files, magnifying glass motif
heading: OFFICIAL INVESTIGATIONS CLOSED ALL OF THESE CASES. PEOPLE STILL DON'T BELIEVE IT.
photo_note: Use a designed graphic/collage rather than any real photo — combines symbolic elements (file folders, a magnifying glass) with no real faces.
confirmed: Across JFK, Diana, and Marilyn Monroe, official government or judicial bodies conducted formal investigations and reached conclusions — yet each case remains widely associated with 'unsolved mystery' status in public perception.
disputed: Researchers studying conspiracy belief point to a consistent pattern: documented irregularities (missing files, conflicts of interest, sealed records) are real in nearly every case — but those irregularities get interpreted as proof of a cover-up rather than ordinary bureaucratic failure, which is statistically the more common explanation. Distinguishing 'there are real unanswered questions' from 'this proves a conspiracy' is the central skill this series has tried to model all week.
caption:
JFK. Diana. Marilyn Monroe. MLK. Tupac. Official investigations existed for every one of these cases — yet all of them remain associated with 'unsolved mystery' status in public perception.

The pattern: documented irregularities are real in nearly every case (missing files, conflicts of interest, sealed records). **But those irregularities being real doesn't automatically prove a deliberate cover-up — bureaucratic failure is statistically the more common explanation, even when it doesn't feel as satisfying.**
